previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient with a complex medical history including end-stage renal disease, antiphospholipid syndrome, systemic lupus erythematosus, and seizure disorder was admitted for abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and weakness. Imaging revealed significant fecal loading and findings consistent with mild ileus likely due to gastroenteritis and poor oral intake. She was treated with an aggressive bowel regimen and hemodialysis, which resolved her hyperkalemia and improved her symptoms. Her shoulder pain was attributed to bursitis and managed conservatively. She remained stable throughout the admission, with improvement in abdominal symptoms and normalization of electrolytes. She was discharged home with instructions to continue laxatives, resume her regular medications including macitentan, and follow up with her specialists.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ w/PMHx of SLE w/ thrombotic 
microangiopathy, TTP, ESRD s/p failed transplant in ___ now on 
___ HD, APLS and prior DVT on warfarin, PAH, and seizure 
disorder who p/w anterior epistaxis, stabilized with 
nasopharygeal packing. Pt w/hx of sinusitis and intermittent 
epistaxis historically controlled by pressure. In the ED ENT was 
consulted and cautery was attempted but was unsuccessful, nasal 
packing was placed and the bleeding stopped. Clindamycin was 
started PPX. ENT re-examined the patient and removed the 
packing, on rhinoscopy no signs of bleeding were found. As pt 
w/sig bleeding and clotting hx, was monitored o/n after packing 
removed, no further bleeding occurred. Also had a make up HD 
session and was restored to her MWF HD schedule, which she 
tolerated.

ACTIVE ISSUES
=============
# Epistaxis. In the setting of warfarin usage. Packed in ED with 
cessation of bleeding. ENT saw pt, saw no e/o active bleeding on 
rhinoscopy, removed packing and recommended DC'ing ABx ppx. No 
current recurrent epistaxis. Gave recommendations to help 
prevent epistaxis. Discussed with pt's Heme team, who 
recommended goal INR 2.0, as more concerned about thrombosis 
over bleeding. Warfarin was held on ___ w/INR of 2.5, trended 
down to 1.3, per pt's AC monitor, pt will hold Warfarin on night 
of DC. Will f/u with outpatient ENT, given Afrin for when nasal 
bleeding recurs and instructions on what to do when this happens 
again. Will also f/u with outpatient Heme.

# ESRD: HD MWF. No evidence of volume overload on exam. 
Continued home sevelamer. Had extra HD session over admission 
for a catch up session.

# Abdominal Pain: Likely secondary to cathartic effect of 
swallowing blood. Abdomen exam currently benign. RESOLVED.

CHRONIC ISSUES  
==============
# Antiphopholipid syndrome / Hyperfibrinolytic syndrome - On 
warfarin as outpatient with goal INR 1.5-2.5, managed by her 
nephrologist, INR on admission 2.3, was 1.3 on day of DC, will 
adjust dosing per OSH nephrologist
 
# Pulmonary arterial hypertension - Demonstrated on RHC in 
___. On endothelin antagonist with Macitentan with 
improvement in her symptoms and functional capacity per 
pulmonology. Recent PFTs ___ demonstrated an FVC of 1.8 
liters, 70% predicted; FEV1 1.42 liters, 72% predicted, ratio of 
79%.  Continued macitentan 10 mg daily (may take own medication) 


# Anemia - Chronic, normocytic anemia ___ to ESRD.  Presented 
with H&H slightly down from baseline, H&H stable over admission, 
DC H&H 10.5/32.9 at current baseline.     

# Hypertension. Previously on amlodipine and labetalol 100 mg 
bid. Currently on no anti-hypertensives, was not required over 
admission

# GERD/esophageal dysmotility. Chronic and long-standing; has 
been worked up previously with endoscopy and has been treated 
with anti-spasmodics, but she is not currently taking these. 
Continued home ranitidine and omeprazole  
# OSA: To continue home CPAP once nose bleed resolved  
# Seizure disorder: Continued home lamotrigine, topamax 
# Chronic pain: Continued home dilaudid 
# Glaucoma: Continued home latanoprost and rewetting drops

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES
===================
-Pt seen by ENT, given instructions for how to handle nose 
bleeds in the future, including 3d of Afrin and applying 
pressure for 30 mins w/o stopping. Also given techniques from 
ENT to help reduce the chance of rebleeding. f/u apt with pt's 
ENT doctor scheduled for ___ week f/u
-Pt's Coumadin was held over admission, Heme team was contacted, 
preferred that pt remain AC'd with goal INR as close to 2.0 as 
possible. INR on DC was 1.3. F/U apt made with Dr. ___ 
would not be recommended in the future per Heme team. Warfarin 
managed per Dr. ___ will follow his recs for Coumadin 
dosing

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

You were admitted after you were found to have a nosebleed at 
home that wouldn't stop. In the emergency room your nose was 
packed with rhinorocket that helped to ""tamponade"" (stop) the 
bleeding. You also received several doses of clindamycin while 
the packing was in place to prevent infections. Our ENT doctors 
saw ___ and removed the packing. You had no further bleeding and 
on inspection of your nasal cavity they did not find any signs 
of bleeding. We gave you afrin nasal spray to use in case you 
have any more bleeding, and also recommended that you apply 
pressure to your nose for 30 minutes (and don't lean back!). We 
made you an appointment with Dr. ___ you would like to 
follow up with him, as well as with your ENT doctor. We held 
your Coumadin while you were here because of your bleeding.

Please remember to weigh yourself every morning, and to call an 
MD if your weight goes up more than 3 lbs.

It was a pleasure taking care of you!

Your ___ Team
